articles.title: Estimating malaria burden in sub-Saharan Africa under intervention disruption using satellite-derived representations
articles.titleEn: Estimating malaria burden in sub-Saharan Africa under intervention disruption using satellite-derived representations
articles.abstract: Malaria remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. Stalled progress and funding constraints raise important questions about the dependence of current malaria burden on sustained intervention coverage. Here, we estimate malaria transmission potential under a low-intervention scenario where major malaria interventions are withdrawn while broader ecological and demographic conditions remain constant. We develop a contrastive representation-learning framework applied to 30-m Landsat 8 satellite imagery, integrating the resulting environmental representations within a Bayesian hierarchical model. This approach improves predictive accuracy over existing covariate-based malaria mapping methods. Using contemporary Global Burden of Disease 2024 population estimates, we estimate an annual malaria burden of 422 (275-582) million cases across sub-Saharan Africa, representing a 131% increase relative to current estimates. These findings quantify the structural vulnerability of malaria control gains across sub-Saharan Africa and reveal where intervention disruption could have the greatest impact.

articles.title: Evidence for p-wave magnetism in electronic band structure of metallic EuSi
articles.titleEn: Evidence for p-wave magnetism in electronic band structure of metallic EuSi
articles.abstract: One active frontier of quantum-matter research is the realization of p -wave symmetry-breaking phases in fermionic systems, long exemplified by the A phase of superfluid helium-3 (refs. 1–3 ). Achieving p -wave superconductivity 4 and its magnetic analogue 5 —characterized by a time-reversal-symmetric, p -wave spin-polarized Fermi surface—remains a grand challenge 6,7 . Despite recent progress in identifying candidate p -wave magnets 5,7–10 , spin-resolved spectroscopic evidence for their electronic structures remains limited. Here we report angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and spin-ARPES evidence for p -wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi, supported by symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations and neutron scattering. Neutron diffraction reveals a chiral spiral phase between 33.4 K and 62 K that fulfils archetypal p -wave magnetism criteria: it preserves the combined symmetry of time reversal and lattice translation, while breaking inversion symmetry. Spin-integrated ARPES reveals a pronounced magnetism-driven reconstruction of the electronic structure, with energy separations exceeding 100 meV, and spin-ARPES resolves S y polarization in near-Fermi-level spectral features. The extracted S y exhibits a sign-changing modulation across successive magnetic Brillouin zones and is suppressed near the nodal regions, consistent with the predicted p -wave spin texture and unfolded spin-polarization calculations. Magnetic force microscopy and micro-ARPES further reveal approximately 10-μm chiral magnetic domains. These results identify EuSi as a stoichiometric metallic platform for investigating p -wave magnetism in electronic band structures and spin-symmetry-based functionalities in spintronics 10 , topological matter 7 , superconductivity 11 and beyond.

articles.title: Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene
articles.titleEn: Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene
articles.abstract: van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies 1–4 . Because the interfaces are not covalently bonded, the constituent crystals can slide, rotate and reconstruct, resulting in several possible competing structural phases 2,5,6 . However, controlled tuning of this balance, and hence dynamical control over the stacking, has yet to be achieved. Here we report a dynamical heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (mhBN) on either side. In such a system, a global structural phase transition, manifested as a change of crystalline symmetry observed by scanning tunnelling microscopy, could be induced by gating, magnetic field or temperature. This structural transition is accompanied by an exotic electronic transition: the doping of graphene switches between discrete levels, corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons or holes per moiré plaquette. We attribute this integer doping to charge trapping in localized, strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (flat bands in reciprocal space 7–12 ), produced by moiré reconstruction (strongly enhanced by the mhBN). Electrical control of coupled structural and electronic phase transitions provides a route to engineering strain-induced flat bands and strain–Coulomb correlations in van der Waals heterostructures.

articles.title: Ferroptosis in cancer cells triggers PGE2 production for tumour immune escape
articles.titleEn: Ferroptosis in cancer cells triggers PGE2 production for tumour immune escape
articles.abstract: Ferroptosis, a form of cell death induced by overwhelming membrane lipid peroxidation, is a vulnerability of many cancers, including cancers resistant to current molecular and immune-based therapies 1–7 . Triggering of ferroptosis therefore provides an opportunity to achieve elimination of difficult-to-treat cancers 1–4,8,9 . Studies in mouse cancer models have demonstrated that anticancer immunity, mediated by dendritic cells (DCs) and CD8 + T cells, is essential for effective tumour eradication by ferroptosis-inducing strategies 10–13 . However, ferroptotic cells limit this response 8–10,14 , resulting in immune escape and tumour growth through mechanisms that remain unclear. Here we demonstrate that ferroptotic cancer cells activate a molecular program resulting in aberrant production of prostaglandin E 2 (PGE 2 ), which limits the stimulation of anticancer CD8 + T cell responses by type 1 conventional DCs (cDC1s), thereby promoting immune escape. In ferroptotic cancer cells, lipid peroxidation-mediated membrane permeabilization enables Ca 2+ influx, which activates p38 MAPK signalling and thereby drives PGE 2 production. This signalling axis is uncoupled from cancer cell death and can be targeted to selectively interfere with immune-inhibitory PGE 2 production while preserving ferroptotic cancer cell elimination. In the context of cancer cell ferroptosis, ablation of PGE 2 production or disrupting PGE 2 signalling restores cDC1-mediated anticancer CD8 + T cell responses and leads to effective tumour elimination. Our findings identify a key mechanism that limits antitumour immunity and prevents tumour elimination upon ferroptosis induction in cancer cells, which could be exploited for cancer therapy.

articles.title: Injury-induced signalling coordinates immunity and cannibalism in locusts
articles.titleEn: Injury-induced signalling coordinates immunity and cannibalism in locusts
articles.abstract: Cannibalism, the consumption of conspecifics, is widespread across the animal kingdom and can profoundly influence individual fitness and population dynamics 1,2 . Although the ecological and social conditions that favour cannibalism have been well documented 2 , the molecular signals that trigger cannibalistic attacks have remained poorly understood. Here we show that in Locusta migratoria , guaiacol, a volatile compound with augmented release after injury, attracts gregarious nymphs and induces cannibalistic behaviour. Guaiacol is detected by olfactory receptors LmOR36 and LmOR34, and disruption of either receptor abolishes attraction, thereby impairing induction of cannibalism. Guaiacol is synthesized by haemolymph symbiont Enterobacter hormaechei . Injury promotes bacterial congregation at the wound site, leading to elevated guaiacol production through a clustered set of vanillic acid decarboxylase genes; deletion of this gene cluster abolishes guaiacol production and its behavioural effects. Notably, guaiacol initially functions as a beneficial signal after injury. Guaiacol activates immune-related pathways in wounded locusts, enhancing pathogen resistance and increasing survival following minor injury. However, when guaiacol emission exceeds a threshold determined by injury severity, it functions as an external cue that attracts cannibals. Cannibalistic locusts exploit this immune-related odour to locate severely injured conspecifics, gaining both nutritional resources and immune system benefits. Together, our findings identify a microbial–chemical mechanism that links immune defence with cannibalistic behaviour and provide potential molecular targets for manipulation of cannibalism-dependent population dynamics.

articles.title: Analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions
articles.titleEn: Analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions
articles.abstract: Quantum field theories provide fundamental models of complex interacting systems 1–3 , from high-energy physics and cosmology to condensed matter. However, solving these models in non-perturbative and dynamical regimes is often challenging, particularly in more than one spatial dimension. Analogue simulation using tunable synthetic quantum systems can both verify existing theoretical predictions and lead to physical insights. Here we realize analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions (two spatial dimensions and time), using two coherently coupled spin components 4,5 in a uniform two-dimensional atomic Bose–Einstein condensate 6,7 . Specifically, we encode the paradigmatic sine-Gordon model 8,9 in the long-wavelength modes of the field describing the relative phase, ϕ , of the two components. In the perturbative regime, collective field excitations exhibit a relativistic dispersion with a tunable mass gap. We also observe explicitly non-perturbative phenomena, including the existence of topological domain walls across which ϕ rapidly winds by 2π (ref. 10 ). Our work opens possibilities for studies of cosmologically relevant phenomena including preheating 11,12 , dynamics of topological defects 13,14 and relativistic false-vacuum decay 15–19 .

articles.title: Fully integrated perovskite active polaritonic circuits
articles.titleEn: Fully integrated perovskite active polaritonic circuits
articles.abstract: Photonic integrated circuits are emerging as a key technology for compact, analogue and energy-efficient optical information processing 1 . Yet, their practical implementation remains limited by the intrinsically weak optical nonlinearities of conventional materials, which demand high power and large device footprints to achieve substantial nonlinear responses 2 . Exciton–polaritons, hybrid light–matter excitations of semiconducting materials, offer a promising route to overcome these limitations by combining strong optical nonlinearities with the high speed and scalability typical of photonic platforms 3–5 . However, despite their potential, fully integrated on-chip polaritonic systems simultaneously delivering room-temperature waveguide lasing, controllable optical routing and amplification have remained elusive. Here we demonstrate a fully integrated perovskite polaritonic circuit that brings these functionalities together in a single-step-grown platform. We realize precise and scalable polariton circuits with integrated gratings that act as both couplers and reflectors, enabling in-plane Fabry–Pérot cavities. These structures support robust in-plane polariton lasing with coherent guided emission at a geometry-defined wavelength, optical amplification of propagating polaritons and nonlinear optical phase control exceeding π, all within the same on-chip architecture. Our results establish perovskite polariton circuits as a scalable platform for active and interferometric integrated photonics.

articles.title: Tropical land-use intensification restructures biodiversity
articles.titleEn: Tropical land-use intensification restructures biodiversity
articles.abstract: Tropical land-use intensification threatens global biodiversity, yet most assessments of tropical agricultural landscapes focus on local-scale biodiversity, overlooking how land use restructures biodiversity across space and multiple taxa. Here we provide an ecosystem-wide assessment of 24 taxonomic groups across all domains of life—encompassing 40,049 species—along a land-use intensification gradient from lowland forests to intensively managed smallholder cash-crop monocultures in Indonesian landscapes. Despite widespread losses of landscape and local multidiversity 1 in monocultures (approximately 78% and 50%, respectively), we found no evidence for consistent community homogenization with land-use intensification. Instead, monocultures exhibit a systematic shift from turnover to nestedness for aboveground taxa. Such patterns of differentiation may mask trajectories towards biotic homogenization via early stages of assemblage simplification. Biotic differentiation has the potential to partly mitigate biodiversity losses by positively affecting γ-diversity. This opens management options, including the conservation of existing remnants of traditional agriculture and the implementation of sustainable management practices 2–4 . Our results demonstrate that tropical land-use intensification restructures biodiversity not only through species loss, but also via a pervasive reorganization of community composition across trophic levels. Conserving tropical biodiversity, therefore, requires a multi-taxon, landscape-scale perspective that explicitly integrates agricultural land uses with the protection of natural and semi-natural habitats to reconcile agricultural production and conservation.

articles.title: Localized end-on heating for hot spot ignition in precompressed isochoric plasmas
articles.titleEn: Localized end-on heating for hot spot ignition in precompressed isochoric plasmas
articles.abstract: In fast ignition inertial confinement fusion, a “heating cone” is employed to shorten the transport distance of the relativistic electron beam (REB) to the high-density plasma core, thereby mitigating energy losses at the plasma edge. However, its insertion depth and survival time are constrained by the sustained pressure from the large-scale plasma edge during the implosion process. Our whole-process simulations demonstrated that, in the double-cone ignition scheme, the head-on collision of two deuterium-tritium plasma jets not only forms a high-density plateau with a small-scale edge, but also substantially reduces the interaction time between the heating cone and the colliding plasma to approximately 0.1 ns . This shortened interaction time enables the heating cone to remain intact after the peak compression, even when placed directly at the small-scale edge of the colliding plasma. The small-scale edge is compatible with the range of the soft-spectrum REB generated by the heating lasers. Such a REB efficiently heats a localized end-on hot spot adjacent to the high-density plateau, guided by a kT-level magnetic field amplified from a seed field during the collision process. Ignited by the localized hot spot, the high-density plateau can undergo sufficient burning and achieve a fusion energy gain of 6.8 using 60 kJ heating lasers.

articles.title: ATAT1-dependent microtubule acetylation drives pancreatic tumorigenesis through DNMT1-mediated regulation of NDRG4
articles.titleEn: ATAT1-dependent microtubule acetylation drives pancreatic tumorigenesis through DNMT1-mediated regulation of NDRG4
articles.abstract: Microtubule (MT) acetylation is frequently elevated in cancer and associated with poor prognosis. Alpha-tubulin acetyltransferase 1 (ATAT1), the principal enzyme responsible for this modification, has therefore emerged as a potential therapeutic target. However, which cancer types depend on ATAT1 activity and are selectively vulnerable to its inhibition remains unclear. Here, using a phospho-specific marker of ATAT1 activity, we identify pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) as an ATAT1-dependent malignancy. ATAT1 activity is elevated in human PDAC and genetically engineered mouse models, emerging during pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia and persisting in a substantial subset of tumors. Genetic inactivation or pharmacologic inhibition of ATAT1 suppresses PDAC cell growth, reduces orthotopic tumor burden, and markedly inhibits tumor initiation in KPC mice without overt toxicity. Mechanistically, ATAT1-dependent MT acetylation sustains Akt signaling, resulting in inhibitory phosphorylation of GSK3β and stabilization of the DNA methyltransferase DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1). Elevated DNMT1 promotes repression of tumor suppressor genes, including NDRG4, whereas inhibition of ATAT1 or DNMT1 restores NDRG4 expression and impairs tumor growth. Together, these findings identify a previously unrecognized ATAT1-Akt-GSK3β-DNMT1 signaling axis linking cytoskeletal acetylation to NDRG4 repression and reveal ATAT1 as a therapeutic vulnerability during the early stages of pancreatic tumorigenesis.

articles.title: Paul R. Ehrlich: Visionary pioneer and public scientist for nature and humanity
articles.titleEn: Paul R. Ehrlich: Visionary pioneer and public scientist for nature and humanity
articles.abstract: Paul R. Ehrlich is legendary for his scientific insight and impact—and even more so for bringing science to the public through writing, speaking, and, most famously, twenty-some appearances on the Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson. He was quick-witted—he would readily add quick-tempered, with chagrin—and could bring down a house. Paul cherished deep friendships and nature. He loved collaborating with his wife of 71 years, Anne H. Ehrlich, and with innumerable students and colleagues all over the world. He made transformative contributions of astonishing range, including in ecology and evolution, biodiversity and conservation, human population and overconsumption, and the integration of ecology and economics. He was deeply committed to racial and social justice, reflected in his actions and writing.

articles.title: Overlooked biodiversity hotspots revealed by a pluralistic approach for quantifying amphibian biodiscovery needs
articles.titleEn: Overlooked biodiversity hotspots revealed by a pluralistic approach for quantifying amphibian biodiscovery needs
articles.abstract: Undocumented and poorly known species spanning Linnean and Wallacean biodiversity shortfalls pose a major challenge to conservation due to the uncertainty they introduce. To address this, we developed a novel pluralistic approach that accounts for sampling gaps, spatial patterns, environmental associations, and varying conservation needs simultaneously, using amphibians as a case study. Using environment-based richness models and species accumulation curves (SACs), we identified areas with high biodiscovery needs for amphibians. These were concentrated primarily in humid tropical South America, sub-Saharan Africa, and East/Southeast Asia. While environmental models produced more reliable richness estimates than SACs overall, SAC-based estimates nonetheless added unique insights, especially in biodiverse, moderately well-sampled areas like Costa Rica and Panama. By integrating environmental models and SACs—thus leveraging combined strengths of previous approaches—our holistic scoring technique also proved consistent in estimating biodiscovery priorities across ecoregions, enabling robust recommendations for future sampling.

articles.title: Niche constraints drive differences between mycorrhizal fungal guilds in future range shifts
articles.titleEn: Niche constraints drive differences between mycorrhizal fungal guilds in future range shifts
articles.abstract: Mycorrhizal fungi are a diverse and ubiquitous group of plant symbionts whose distribution strongly influences ecosystem function across the globe. Yet, until now, we do not have quantitative data on the range sizes of different mycorrhizal fungal taxa, limiting our capacity to forecast future shifts in community composition and function. Here, we use 115,924 DNA sequence-derived observations to map the distribution of 651 common mycorrhizal fungal taxa and forecast future changes to their range sizes. We demonstrate that climate, plant cover, and soil factors, particularly mean annual temperature, net primary productivity, and soil organic carbon, exert major control over mycorrhizal fungal distributions. Based on these drivers, the ecological niches of mycorrhizal fungi consistently differ between arbuscular and ectomycorrhizal functional guilds. Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal taxa generally occupy a wider niche breadth than ectomycorrhizal fungi, occurring across larger ranges of climate, soil, plant cover, topography, and disturbance conditions. Our models also predict widespread decreases in the suitable range size of mycorrhizal fungal taxa under projected future global climates, with average ranges decreasing by 13.8% or ~2.2 million km 2 under high emissions scenarios (ssp5-8.5). This decrease in projected range size will be most pronounced for ectomycorrhizal fungi, strongly linked to constraints from their smaller overall niches. By generating a global atlas of common mycorrhizal fungi and their associated environmental niche, we establish a critical baseline for widely suspected declines in global fungal biodiversity.

This decrease in projected range size will be most pronounced for ectomycorrhizal fungi, strongly linked to constraints from their smaller overall niches. By generating a global atlas of common mycorrhizal fungi and their associated environmental niche, we establish a critical baseline for widely suspected declines in global fungal biodiversity.

articles.title: Basal radial glia abundance and morphotype diversity in the hippocampal dentate gyrus imply their evolutionarily ancient origin
articles.titleEn: Basal radial glia abundance and morphotype diversity in the hippocampal dentate gyrus imply their evolutionarily ancient origin
articles.abstract: Basal radial glia (bRG) are neural progenitor cells (NPCs) essential for primate neocortical expansion, but their presence in other brain regions and across species remains poorly understood. Here, we show that the developing mouse dentate gyrus (DG), unlike the neocortex, harbors abundant NPCs that transcriptionally and morphologically resemble human neocortical bRG. This striking abundance is conserved across other Boreoeutherian species, including mice, marmosets, ferrets, and pigs. Comparative transcriptomics uncovered a shared morphoregulatory gene signature between bRG in mouse DG and human neocortex. Immunohistochemical analysis showed diversity in DG bRG morphotypes across species. Remarkably, compared to the neocortex, DG bRG consistently exhibit greater morphotype diversity. Ancestral state reconstruction suggests that this diversity was already present in the common ancestor of Boreoeutherians. Together, our findings position the DG as a conserved, evolutionarily ancient niche for bRG, revealing that region- and species-specific adaptations of NPCs extend beyond the neocortex.

articles.title: Hydromorphodynamic Impacts Extend Beyond the Recirculation Zone of a Spur Dike on a Mobile Bed
articles.titleEn: Hydromorphodynamic Impacts Extend Beyond the Recirculation Zone of a Spur Dike on a Mobile Bed
articles.abstract: Spur dikes generate a recirculation zone, and reattachment length is used to estimate hydraulic effects and guide structure spacing. Fixed‐bed studies of non‐submerged, impermeable spur dikes commonly report primary recirculation lengths on the order of 10 dike lengths, but direct measurements over deformed mobile beds remain sparse. We test whether the end of the recirculation region also marks the end of the downstream flow and bed response. We analyze a 32‐day clear‐water mobile‐bed flume experiment with post‐run three‐component velocity measurements and a final bed survey. Across two elevations and two criteria, estimates of the primary reverse‐flow extent span 1.00–2.68 dike lengths. At the same measured locations in each included section, the difference from the upstream velocity field reached a local minimum at eight dike lengths, then increased, with later values above the comparison level through 16 dike lengths. The farther downstream reach contained an oblique depositional macroform and about 96% of the mapped deposition. At the final velocity section, 20 dike lengths downstream, the streamwise momentum‐flux centroid on the common coordinates was displaced toward the structure side, having reversed between 12 and 16 dike lengths, while the lower part of the flow still showed momentum deficit, elevated turbulence, and secondary circulation. Structure‐side bed deformation extended to the survey limit at 24 dike lengths. In this experiment, the primary recirculation region was therefore short relative to the longer reach of altered flow and bed topography. Reattachment length alone did not describe the full downstream response of the mobile‐bed channel.

articles.title: Observation‐Anchored Machine Learning for Baseflow Estimation in India
articles.titleEn: Observation‐Anchored Machine Learning for Baseflow Estimation in India
articles.abstract: Baseflow is critical for maintaining river flows, supporting ecosystems, and meeting water demands during dry periods. Yet, large‐scale estimation of baseflow remains challenging due to the lack of direct observations. Here, we present HyGBR‐Baseflow, a machine learning framework that estimates baseflow by anchoring the learning to reference points (RPs) and read directly from streamflow recession. The framework uses four graphical and five digital filter methods as predictors, together with hydrometeorological variables. To address the scarcity of reliable training data during monsoon season, our framework uses pseudo‐reference points (PRPs), derived from the mean baseflow of the three best‐performing baseflow separation methods and assigns reduced sample weights (0.2–0.5) compared to true RPs. We applied HyGBR‐Baseflow to 227 stations across 18 major Indian River basins for 1961–2021 and evaluated its performance using Nash–Sutcliffe Efficiency, Kling–Gupta Efficiency, refined index of agreement, and R 2 . Overall, the HyGBR‐Baseflow framework consistently outperformed individual baseflow separation methods, with the largest improvements during the monsoon season across diverse hydrological regimes. The baseflow trend analysis showed pronounced declines in several catchments. Even the Ganga and Brahmaputra basins, which comprise catchments where baseflow contributes more than 70% of the total streamflow at most stations, showed declining baseflow trends. Additionally, the long‐term baseflow index indicated higher baseflow contributions in humid catchments compared to semi‐arid and dry sub‐humid regions. The HyGBR‐Baseflow provides a scalable, accurate, and observation‐anchored nonlinear reconciliation framework for baseflow estimation that can support groundwater–surface water interaction studies, water resources planning, drought monitoring, and climate change impact assessments across India.

articles.title: Identifying Dominant Environmental Predictors of Coastal Shallow Groundwater Levels Across Diel to Seasonal Time Scales
articles.titleEn: Identifying Dominant Environmental Predictors of Coastal Shallow Groundwater Levels Across Diel to Seasonal Time Scales
articles.abstract: Coastal zone, especially mega‐deltas are densely populated and socioeconomically important, where shallow groundwater responds to interacting terrestrial, marine, atmospheric and engineered influences across multiple time scales, contributing to uncertainty in groundwater prediction. Here, we utilized a multiscale information‐theoretic diagnostic framework to analyze groundwater‐level (GWL) dynamics in the Yellow River Delta and to identifying dominant environmental predictors of coastal shallow groundwater levels across diel to seasonal time scales. Results indicate that: (a) the seasonal component dominates GWL variability, accounting for 73% of total variance. Air temperature ( T ) serves as the primary predictor at sites closer to the coastline, whereas precipitation ( P ) dominates at sites farther inland. Seasonal GWL is asynchronous with T and P, with offsets of 27 ± 23 and 13 days, respectively. (b) the multiday component accounts for 25% of total variance; here, evaporative demand drives recession dynamics, while P induces episodic recharge pulses (lag: 1.1 ± 0.25 days). (c) the diel component (2% of variance) exhibits regular diel cycles. P outperforms potential evapotranspiration (PET) as the dominant predictor, suggesting that rapid infiltration events generate intense high‐frequency hydraulic signals that outweigh regular diel evapotranspiration oscillations in information content. Near tidal channels, tides dominate, with GWL lagging tidal stage by 4 hr. By explicitly resolving time‐scale dependence, asynchrony, and nonlinearity, this study advances the understanding of coastal shallow GWL dynamics and provides a basis for GWL prediction, model development, and coastal groundwater management.

articles.title: Equity and Effectiveness of Groundwater Governance Policies
articles.titleEn: Equity and Effectiveness of Groundwater Governance Policies
articles.abstract: Groundwater depletion threatens the sustainability of irrigated agriculture worldwide, particularly in regions where aquifers provide the primary or only irrigation source. While many policies have been designed to reduce pumping, previous studies have emphasized hydrologic effectiveness or average regional economic outcomes, with less attention to how groundwater‐policy costs and benefits are distributed among farmers. This study uses an agent‐based modeling framework to systematically compare six groundwater governance approaches: uniform pumping restrictions, volumetric pumping fees with and without revenue recycling through groundwater conservation payments, two priority‐based allocation systems, and a priority‐weighted pumping restriction system. Across various climate and market conditions, we designed each policy to meet the same groundwater‐stabilization goal, allowing a fair and direct evaluation of both aquifer dynamics and the distribution of farm‐level profits. When each policy was set to meet a common groundwater stabilization goal, they created very different economic outcomes for farmers. Policies that apply the same allocation to all irrigators or scale allocations by seniority produced the most balanced results. Fee‐based pumping generated consistent but uniformly lower profits, while recycling fees as payments to farmers who forgo irrigation improved profitability and equity. By contrast, policies that strictly enforce water‐rights seniority created an economic divide: senior users with water access maintained high earnings while junior farmers had little or no access to irrigation water. These findings highlight that considering both sustainability and distributive economic consequences provides a stronger foundation for evaluating and designing groundwater management policies that balance aquifer conservation with the economic well‐being of producers.

articles.title: Assessing the contribution of extratropical cyclones to river floods that caused property damage in Quebec, Canada
articles.titleEn: Assessing the contribution of extratropical cyclones to river floods that caused property damage in Quebec, Canada
articles.abstract: In the past few decades, the province of Quebec in eastern Canada has experienced widespread and costly flood events, yet the contribution of extratropical cyclones to these floods remains unquantified. This paper presents a methodology for analysing the contribution of extratropical cyclones (ETCs) to 498 fluvial floods that occurred in watersheds in southern Quebec, Canada, between 1991 and 2020, and highlights key characteristics shared by the 200 flood ETCs (storms that contributed to flooding) identified in the study. This analysis combined reconstituted river outputs, government financial aid claims following flooding, ETC tracks, and precipitation data to identify flood events and their relevant ETCs. ETC contribution was defined as the percentage of rainfall during a search window surrounding each flood event that was associated with the relevant ETCs. Most of these floods occurred in the spring (74.7 %). The majority (72.7 %) of flood events had a high (50 %–75 %) to very high (>75 %) ETC contribution, and only 2.6 % of events (mostly occurring in summer) had a negligible ( Baseline Southern Quebec domain , N =6027). Flood ETCs also spent on average 18.2 h more in the domain and generally tracked over southern Quebec as opposed to over the Atlantic Ocean along the east coast of North America or over northern Quebec like non-flood ETCs. The percentages of financial aid claims allotted to flood ETCs were highly variable. Just five of the 200 flood ETCs were associated with 51.0 % of all financial aid claims filed during the 30-year period, indicating that a high to very high ETC contribution rarely resulted in widespread flooding. The method developed in this study could be applied to other regions or types of storms analysed (e.g. tropical cyclones and mesoscale convective systems) to further our understanding of the atmospheric causes of flooding in northeastern North America.

articles.title: Process diagnostics of snowmelt runoff in global hydrological and land surface models – Part 2: Are more complex models better?
articles.titleEn: Process diagnostics of snowmelt runoff in global hydrological and land surface models – Part 2: Are more complex models better?
articles.abstract: The added value of increased process complexity has long been a central yet unresolved question in hydrological modeling, particularly for snowmelt runoff (SMR), where multiple physical processes interact in complex ways. In this study, we develop a Tree-Based Model Complexity Scoring (TBMCS) method to quantify the complexity of snow-related processes across 13 global hydrological and land surface models. We then systematically revisit the important linkage between model complexity and model performance in three distinct SMR characteristics, i.e., total runoff ( Q sum ), peak flow ( Q max ), and centroid timing (CTQ) of runoff in the snowmelt period. Further, we assess how the basin complexity (as delineated by 1455 snow-dominated basins), forcing difference and calibration status can modulate this linkage. Results show that (1) models differ substantially in their physical process representations, with the largest divergence in melting process treatments, followed by sublimation, interception and rainfall-snowfall partitioning processes. (2) Model performance for Q sum and Q max shows only weak associations with model complexity. Interestingly, we find a positive correlation between snow-process complexity and model performance for CTQ ( r =0.32). articles.title: Benefits of multi-target and self-supervised LSTM models for water quantity and quality
articles.titleEn: Benefits of multi-target and self-supervised LSTM models for water quantity and quality
articles.abstract: Deep learning has become a standard tool for streamflow modelling, but its application to water quality remains challenging due to sparse, irregular, and noisy in-situ observations. Yet, water-quality variables are tightly linked to discharge and to each other through shared hydrological and biogeochemical controls, suggesting that jointly modelling water quantity and quality may help compensate for limited data availability. In this study, we compare single-target, multi-target, and self-supervised LSTM models for the joint simulation of discharge and six water-quality variables (NO 3 -N, PO 4 -P, DO, DOC, EC, and WT) across 408 German catchments. Our results highlight that extending the baseline LSTM from single-target discharge prediction to jointly predicting discharge and all six water-quality variables does not substantially degrade discharge performance (across all baseline configurations, median KGE ′ = 0.84–0.87) and yields median KGE ′ values between 0.40 (PO 4 -P) and 0.95 (WT) for the water-quality targets. Interestingly, learning discharge as a co-target matches or exceeds the performance of using observed discharge as an additional input for five of the six water-quality variables, with the clearest gain for DOC (ΔKGE ′ = +0.05). This indicates that jointly learning water quantity and quality can be more effective than using discharge as a predictor. A variable-averaged loss function is key to balance the strongly uneven observation densities of discharge and water-quality variables. Building on this multi-target framework, we further explore whether an alternative training strategy based on self-supervised learning can better exploit the incomplete and heterogeneous nature of environmental observations. Our evaluation reveals that the self-supervised LSTM yields a level of predictive skill comparable to the multi-target supervised baseline LSTM under inference conditions restricted to meteorological drivers and when contextual water-quality data is provided. Thus, while matching the baseline's skill, the self-supervised LSTM gains versatility, as a single model can be applied to many different combinations of available input data without retraining. Besides showcasing the strong performance of LSTMs in water-quality simulations with sparse and irregular data, our results demonstrate that multi-target learning provides an effective framework for coupled water quantity–quality modelling, while self-supervised learning offers additional flexibility for exploiting incomplete and heterogeneous environmental observations.

articles.title: GPU-accelerated atmospheric chemical kinetics using single precision in the ECHAM/MESSy (EMAC) model v2.55 with MEDINA v2.0
articles.titleEn: GPU-accelerated atmospheric chemical kinetics using single precision in the ECHAM/MESSy (EMAC) model v2.55 with MEDINA v2.0
articles.abstract: Atmospheric chemical kinetics puts a major computational burden on Earth system models, yet its embarrassingly parallel nature of the problem structure makes it well suited to GPU acceleration. Here we present a single-precision floating point (FP32) GPU implementation of the MECCA chemical kinetics submodule in the ECHAM/MESSy Atmospheric Chemistry (EMAC) model. It is enabled by the MEDINA code-to-code compiler v2.0 and compatible with the Rosenbrock-family numerical solvers generated by the Kinetic Pre-Processor (KPP). The approach exploits FP32 arithmetic inside the GPU kernels while preserving double precision in the host EMAC workflow via explicit type conversion on the GPU. We evaluate the numerical fidelity and achieved performance in both an idealised box-model configuration and in full EMAC production simulations on the JUWELS Booster system. Across tested mechanisms and resolutions, FP32 reproduces the double-precision CPU reference to within

articles.title: A new high-resolution daily mean South China Sea Ocean Reanalysis dataset: SCSORA
articles.titleEn: A new high-resolution daily mean South China Sea Ocean Reanalysis dataset: SCSORA
articles.abstract: High-resolution three-dimensional (3D) ocean reanalysis data are essential for investigating multiscale ocean dynamics in the regional ocean and their impacts on energy transport, marine ecosystems, and climate change. The South China Sea (SCS), as one of the most eddy-active marginal seas in the global ocean, is characterized by complex 3D dynamical processes and frequent extreme ocean events, imposing urgent data demands on the scientific community. This paper presents a new South China Sea Ocean Reanalysis (SCSORA) dataset, with high resolution (1/30°) covering the period 2001–2024, which is generated by the second version of the SCS Operational Oceanography Forecast System (SCSOFSv2). SCSORA provides daily 3D fields of temperature, salinity, and current velocity, together with sea surface height (SSH). Three categories of observational data are assimilated into SCSOFSv2, including satellite-derived optimum interpolation sea surface temperature (OISST), along-track sea level anomaly (SLA) from AVISO, and in-situ temperature–salinity Argo profiles. Systematic validations against multisource satellite retrievals, in-situ observations, and existing reanalysis products demonstrates that SCSORA achieves satisfactory accuracy and reliability in reproducing sea surface temperature (RMSE: 0.357 °C relative to OSTIA), SLA (RMSE: 5.9 cm), and subsurface thermohaline structure. Kinetic energy spectral analysis indicates that SCSORA can resolve mesoscale processes and has the potential to resolve part of the submesoscale range. Representative applications demonstrate the capability of SCSORA in characterizing the spatiotemporal features of marine heatwaves (MHWs) in the SCS and in examining the modulation of the 3D structure of MHWs by mesoscale eddies. SCSORA provides a critical 3D data foundation for the physical oceanography and extreme event research communities focusing on the SCS. It is publicly available at https://doi.org/10.12378/geodb.2026.2.005.V1 (Zhu and Zhang, 2026).

articles.title: MacroTraits: a global trait data and information system for marine benthic ecology
articles.titleEn: MacroTraits: a global trait data and information system for marine benthic ecology
articles.abstract: For a long time, biological trait data have been a bottleneck in biodiversity research. Constraints of data unavailability and challenging analytical implementation are still obstacles to the investigation of functional biodiversity patterns. This is especially true in marine zoobenthic ecology where the use of biological traits became common much later than in terrestrial and freshwater ecology. Additionally, most of trait-based marine studies have dominantly been conducted in European waters while large gaps remain in other areas of the world. Therefore, this paper offers a framework to fill this gap by providing the most comprehensive zoobenthic trait data compilation at the global scale. Based on more than 8000 references, 1893 species of marine macro- and megazoobenthos are fully documented for life history, dwelling mode, ecosystem function, habitat and biogeography through 41 traits. Next to this compilation, the paper brings clarifications on research directions by means of these data within the dominant paradigms of modern ecology. In particular, the dichotomous expression that contrasts response and effect traits (i.e. fitness components versus ecosystem function) is emphasised. The database is accessible through an R package in the repository https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24318255 (Beauchard and Soetaert, 2026b) and that facilitates data treatment such as trait selection, cross table construction and label handling.

articles.title: Agricultural land management practices in the conterminous United States from 1980–2023
articles.titleEn: Agricultural land management practices in the conterminous United States from 1980–2023
articles.abstract: Agricultural land management practices affect environmental variables including water quality, carbon and nitrogen cycles, and greenhouse gas emissions. To better understand agricultural land management practices, we compiled a land management history for the conterminous United States (CONUS) from 1980–2023. We used the National Resources Inventory as the basis for our sample-based approach to impute planting and harvest dates, synthetic N fertilizer and manure N and C application rates and timing, tillage systems and intensity, and cover crop adoption on major commodity croplands. We aggregated the imputations to a 0.25° grid and compiled a comprehensive data set detailing the management practices used on agricultural lands across CONUS. From 1980–2023, cotton and spring wheat were planted an average of 12 and 9 d later, respectively, while soybeans were planted an average of 12 d earlier. Nationally, average synthetic N fertilizer rates for corn increased from 122.5 kg N ha −1 in 1980 to 150.9 kg N ha −1 in 2023. Similar increases occurred for cotton and wheat. Synthetic fertilization rates climbed steadily from 1980–2000 and then stabilized from 2000–2023. Conversely, manure N amendment rates increased slowly from 1980–2000 and then more rapidly from 2000–2023. Rates for corn, which had the highest use of manure N amendment, increased from 14.9 to 20.7 kg N ha −1 from 1980–2023. On average, no-till and reduced-till practices for row crops increased by 19.2 % and 26.5 %, respectively, across CONUS, while full till practices decreased by 47.2 %. Cover crop adoption increased across CONUS from 1980–2023, with the highest level of adoption occurring in the Eastern US and covering 10 %–13 % of cropland area in these regions by 2023. The results from this product align with previously published histories, although our work provides a more comprehensive representation of cropland management practices than previous works. Our data set is available on Dryad under public domain license (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23987242, Hoskovec, 2026) and can be used to inform studies of agricultural lands that evaluate processes such as greenhouse gas emissions, environmental impacts, and food production.

articles.title: Verification of coastal enhanced weathering by tracking the dissolution of alkaline minerals: theory and laboratory tests with olivine
articles.titleEn: Verification of coastal enhanced weathering by tracking the dissolution of alkaline minerals: theory and laboratory tests with olivine
articles.abstract: Coastal Enhanced Weathering (CEW) is a marine Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) method that adds ground alkaline minerals to shallow regions of the ocean in order to increase seawater alkalinity, i.e. its capacity for storing atmospheric CO 2 as bicarbonate. While CEW is promising with regard to cost and scalability, it is an uncontained, “open-system” style of CDR, and presents significant challenges to effective measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) of the process. In particular, quantifying how much alkalinity is released from an added amount of mineral is challenging as the minerals dissolve and release alkalinity over wide spatial and long temporal scales. Such quantification is further complicated by the fact that dissolved alkalinity is rapidly diluted below detectable concentrations. Here, we propose an approach to quantify alkalinity formation that relies on solid sediment tracers to track mineral grains underwater and measure how much they have dissolved over time. In theory, the amount of dissolution at any given point in time is proportional to the amount of alkalinity released. Thus, the approach aims to overcome the near impossible detection of alkalinity accumulation in the dissolved phase by tracking the loss of alkaline material in the solid phase. We describe a test of the fundamental aspects of this method including the measurement of the mineral and tracer content of a sediment sample, and the extent to which those measurements correlate with changes in seawater chemistry. While the specific tracer used in this experiment proved unsuitable for this method, we found that olivine dissolution significantly increased alkalinity in seawater compared to control incubators. X-Ray Diffraction (XRD) was able to quantify the change in the olivine in the sediment (albeit with large relative errors) and automated particle counting methods were able to enumerate tracer particles when illuminated under UV-A light. These results are insufficient to fully substantiate this method, but rather serve as an illustration of, and proof-of-principle of, a new approach to measure alkalinity addition to the ocean resulting from CEW deployments. By publishing these findings as a LESSONS (Limitations, Errors, Surprises, Shortcomings, Opportunities for New Science) Report we aim to present and introduce a promising opportunity for new science that we hope will spur a thorough and robust investigation of this method in the broader research community.

articles.title: Superionicity and premelting of iron-rich (Fe,Mg)O at Earth’s core-mantle boundary
articles.titleEn: Superionicity and premelting of iron-rich (Fe,Mg)O at Earth’s core-mantle boundary
articles.abstract: Core-mantle interactions are essential for understanding Earth’s interior dynamics and evolution. Experimental studies reveal that core-mantle reactions produce iron-rich (Fe,Mg)O (periclase‑wüstite solid solution). Here we show that Fe-rich (Fe,Mg)O exhibits pronounced superionic-onset and grain-boundary premelting behavior above ~0.9 T m ( T m : melting temperature). These effects are significant in (Fe x Mg 1-x )O (x > 0.8) under core-mantle boundary (CMB) conditions, causing elastic softening, enhanced elemental transport, and ultra-low viscosity. Enhanced diffusion may facilitate core-mantle reactions and the accumulation of Fe-rich material near the CMB, potentially contributing to a dense basal assemblage. Under mantle flow and/or thermal buoyancy, the low viscosity of connected Fe-rich (Fe,Mg)O could favor deformation and redistribution toward shallower depths. This process may contribute to the formation and evolution of some ultra-low velocity zones (ULVZs). The proposed scenario is consistent with the layered structures and inferred low viscosity of some ULVZs and suggests a potential role for Fe-rich (Fe,Mg)O in core-mantle material exchange and heat transfer.

articles.title: Machine learning-driven regulation of the four-electron LiOH pathway in lithium–oxygen batteries with prolonged cycling
articles.titleEn: Machine learning-driven regulation of the four-electron LiOH pathway in lithium–oxygen batteries with prolonged cycling
articles.abstract: The practical deployment of high-energy-density lithium–oxygen batteries is fundamentally restricted by sluggish oxygen redox kinetics and the instability of discharge intermediates. Here, we report an artificial intelligence-integrated framework leveraging interpretable machine learning and density functional theory to navigate a vast chemical space of thousands of active sites. This approach identifies Ni-Co dual-atom catalysts as a better configuration among the selected elements for orchestrating multi-electron transfer. Theoretical analysis reveals that synergistic electronic coupling between the dual-sites fundamentally reconfigures the d -band center, thereby lowering the thermodynamic barriers for oxygen redox. Moreover, the catalysts enable precise regulation of the reaction pathway, inducing a controllable transition from the conventional two-electron pathway to a four-electron pathway. This shift yields a discharge capacity of ~60,000 mAh g −1 . Beyond its role as a positive electrode catalyst, this architecture functions as a multifunctional interfacial protective layer that stabilizes the lithium metal negative electrode by suppressing dendrite growth. Consequently, the lithium–oxygen system achieves stable lifespan of 2075 cycles under the four-electron pathway with reduced voltage decay. This work establishes a data-guided strategy for the rational design of atomic-scale architecture via artificial intelligence, unlocking the potential of multi-electron oxygen chemistry for lithium–oxygen batteries.

articles.title: Boosting Sensitivity of High-Dimensional Solid-State NMR of Proteins by Optimizing Coherence Transfers
articles.titleEn: Boosting Sensitivity of High-Dimensional Solid-State NMR of Proteins by Optimizing Coherence Transfers
articles.abstract: TROP it or drop it: Owing to fast magic-angle spinning at frequencies above 50 kHz, solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance has evolved as a versatile method to decipher protein structure, dynamics, and chemical properties. While conceptually, higher-dimensional approaches such as 4D and 5D correlation spectra are capable of exceeding the established molecular-weight limitations by ameliorating signal overlap, their intrinsic implications for sensitivity and measurement times required have severely limited these important prospects in practice. Here we show that in high-dimensional experiments, the extensive use of dedicated transverse-mixing optimal control pulses (TROPs) can reduce the necessary measurement time by almost an order of magnitude. TROP’ed non-uniformly sampled experiments not only benefit from a multiplicative sensitivity enhancement in each complex time point due to concomitant transfer of both components of complex signals along multi-step magnetization transfer pathways, but additionally from facilitation of reconstruction with better raw data. Aided by the processing framework provided to future users here, the combination of an extensive use of TROPs with increased dimensionality hence presents itself as highly promising to ameliorate the conventional limitations of solid-state NMR.

articles.title: Low-temperature operation of Ag—C based anodeless all-solid-state pouch cells
articles.titleEn: Low-temperature operation of Ag—C based anodeless all-solid-state pouch cells
articles.abstract: Anodeless all-solid-state batteries with Ag-C interlayers offer high energy density and long cycle life, yet their operation in cold environments remains limited by poorly understood failure mechanisms. Using operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy, cryogenic-cross-section electron microscopy, and X-ray diffraction, we discover that Li-Ag alloying dynamics are highly temperature-dependent: rapid at 45 °C but kinetically suppressed at 5 °C. At low temperatures, suppressed alloying leads to sluggish lithium transport, internal lithium extrusion, interlayer delamination, and rapid capacity decay. We demonstrate that a brief initial charge at 45 °C permanently activates the interlayer via Li-Ag alloy formation, enabling efficient Li transport even at 5 °C. Full pouch cells following this activation protocol retain 87% of their initial capacity after 250 completed cycles following one formation cycle at 5 °C. After 250 cycles at 5 °C, AAP-treated cells delivered approximately three times the discharge capacity of cells cycled with the fixed-temperature protocol. Such in situ electrochemical alloy activation offers a practical and scalable approach to extend anodeless all-solid-state battery performance to sub-ambient temperatures without material redesign.

articles.title: Bicontinuous Fibre Formation via Co-precipitate Attenuated Solvent Transfer Induced Assembly
articles.titleEn: Bicontinuous Fibre Formation via Co-precipitate Attenuated Solvent Transfer Induced Assembly
articles.abstract: Polymer–solvent–nonsolvent mixtures provide a versatile route for fabricating structured materials through liquid–liquid phase separation. In this context, solvent transfer–induced phase separation (STrIPS) enables the continuous formation of bicontinuous fibres, yet the process is often limited by coarsening of pores or collapse within the fibre core, leading to structural inhomogeneity. Here, we advance this strategy through Co-precipitate Attenuated Solvent Transfer induced assembly (CAST), in which amphiphilic species precipitate in situ during solvent exchange and preferentially retained within the polymer rich phase. These precipitates act as a distributed molecular retarding agent that delays domain growth, thereby preserving bicontinuity throughout the fibre cross-section to up to 250 µm. Using a poly (ethylene glycol) diacrylate–ethanol–water system with a phenolic oligomer coprecipitate, we demonstrate that CAST stabilizes the hollow bicontinuous domain structure, extending the attainable specific surface area by ca. 100%. Scattering experiments and molecular dynamics simulations confirm that the precipitating species suppress coarsening by restricting mobility within the phase they occupy. Embedding CAST fibres within polydimethylsiloxane demonstrates lightweight composites with sound mitigation capabilities, highlighting the potential for acoustic applications. CAST thus establishes a versatile route to high-performance porous materials with broad potential for structural, acoustic, and energy applications.

articles.title: Quantum-accurate vibrational and conformational dynamics from small molecules to proteins with machine-learned force fields
articles.titleEn: Quantum-accurate vibrational and conformational dynamics from small molecules to proteins with machine-learned force fields
articles.abstract: Biomolecular thermodynamics and spectroscopy depend on relative conformer energies, local curvatures, and collective dipole fluctuations on the potential-energy surface. Conventional molecular mechanics force fields enable large-scale simulations, but their fixed functional forms can misrepresent infrared intensities, mode character, and environment-dependent vibrational response. Here we assess general-purpose machine-learned force fields by using finite-temperature infrared spectra across small molecules, gas-phase peptides, and monomeric, oligomeric, and solvated protein assemblies. To enable this analysis, we introduce QVib, a dataset of 293 molecules and 1366 conformers, together with peptide amide-band benchmarks and p53 oligomerization-domain models, to evaluate vibrational transferability from DFT references to experimental spectra. Across these systems, machine-learned force fields improve over molecular mechanics in reproducing DFT-level forces, vibrational frequencies, densities of states, mode eigenvectors, conformational energetics, and experimental infrared spectra. Among models with explicit long-range electrostatics, SO3LR provides the best accuracy–cost balance of the models tested here. These results show that machine-learned force-field dynamics can recover collective, environment-dependent vibrational landscapes at near-DFT fidelity, enabling spectroscopically validated biomolecular simulations at force-field-like cost.

articles.title: Global Potential of Agrivoltaics: Agriculture‐First and Radiation‐Limited Analysis
articles.titleEn: Global Potential of Agrivoltaics: Agriculture‐First and Radiation‐Limited Analysis
articles.abstract: With rising global food and energy demand, agrivoltaics offer a viable solution for co‐producing crops and solar electricity on shared land. Despite extensive field‐scale design and optimization studies, a large‐scale, crop‐specific assessment constrained by light availability is still missing. Here, we introduce a radiation‐limited framework that uses growing‐season daily light integral (DLI) to set minimum light budgets for wheat, maize, rice, and soybean, and the agrivoltaics light utilization ratio (ALUR) metric to quantify the surplus light available for photovoltaic (PV) electricity generation. This enables a global first‐order assessment of light availability revealing regional potentials and constraints to agrivoltaic adoption. Four agrivoltaic scenarios were explored by varying the light reserved for the crop: (a) literature‐based crop light targets (SC T,crop ), (b) empirical reference values representing the growing‐season light received across the global distribution of each crop (SC R,crop ), (c) a low reserve favoring electricity generation (SC 20 ; 20 mol m −2 day −1 ), and (d) a conservative reserve favoring food security (SC 40 ; 40 mol m −2 day −1 ). Even under the conservative scenario SC 40 , the total estimated mean global electricity‐generation potential is 109 PWh yr −1 (95% uncertainty interval: 39–190 PWh yr −1 ). The estimated radiation‐based potential is sensitive to the crop‐specific DLI allocation, particularly in India and China, but remains substantial across the United States, Brazil, Argentina, Iran, and Pakistan. These findings suggest that while agrivoltaics are not a “one‐size‐fits‐all” solution, their strategic application can mitigate the land‐use conflict between energy and food production.

articles.title: Simulating Cloud‐Driven Turbulence in Stratocumulus Cloud Systems Over Sea Ice in Weather‐Scale Models
articles.titleEn: Simulating Cloud‐Driven Turbulence in Stratocumulus Cloud Systems Over Sea Ice in Weather‐Scale Models
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: Stratocumulus cloud systems play a fundamental role in the climate system due to their impact on the surface radiation budget and boundary layer structure. One of the challenges in modeling these cloud systems is how to represent sub‐grid processes. This study is focused on evaluating and improving the representation of cloud‐driven sub‐grid turbulence in weather‐scale models over sea ice, where stratocumulus clouds decoupled from surface sources of heat and moisture frequently occur. The planetary boundary layer scheme used in the current NOAA Global Forecast System (GFS) to simulate cloud‐driven turbulence is evaluated in nested limited area simulations of a stratocumulus cloud system in the western Arctic and then tested in a single column model (SCM) using a central Arctic case from the Multidisciplinary drifting Observatory for the Study of Arctic Climate expedition. The inner cloud‐resolving nest is used to evaluate coarser nests. The default configuration of this boundary layer scheme uses a mass flux formulation based on a parameterization of surface‐forced thermal plumes to simulate top‐down mixing in stratocumulus systems forced by cloud‐top radiative cooling. It is demonstrated that when a mixed layer model formulation of sub‐grid cloud‐driven turbulence is used instead of the mass flux scheme, it can reproduce the variability of the cloud‐resolving nest while the mass flux formulation produces significant biases in sub‐grid energy and water fluxes, which produce compensating biases in microphysics. This new formulation for sub‐grid cloud‐driven turbulence is shown to have similar results in an SCM run with a GFS prototype physics suite.

articles.title: Kuroshio Extension warming shaped by Gulf Stream variability via the Arctic atmosphere
articles.titleEn: Kuroshio Extension warming shaped by Gulf Stream variability via the Arctic atmosphere
articles.abstract: Recent unprecedented ocean warming has produced coherent sea surface temperature anomalies across the Northern Hemisphere extratropics. While the tropical Pacific is a natural source of North Pacific variability, the influence of the mid-latitude North Atlantic has remained poorly understood. Here we investigate whether Gulf Stream variability modulates Kuroshio Extension variability using 100-year idealized model simulations. We find that Gulf Stream variability remotely modulates Kuroshio Extension variability, explaining 13% of its internal sea surface temperature variance, whereas we find no evidence that Kuroshio variability similarly modulates the Gulf Stream. Positive Gulf Stream sea surface temperature anomalies excite a Northern Annular Mode-like atmospheric circulation response that weakens the Aleutian Low over the North Pacific. The resulting northward shift of the Kuroshio Extension enhances northward warm-water transport and promotes warming in the western mid-latitude North Pacific. We further show that a high-resolution ocean model is required to properly capture this coupling between Gulf Stream variability and atmospheric circulation, highlighting the importance of western boundary currents and associated oceanic fronts for this interbasin pathway. These findings indicate that North Atlantic variability contributed to the exceptional North Pacific warming during 2020–2024 and may provide a source of decadal predictability for Northern Hemisphere climate.

articles.title: Resilient j = 3/2 superconductivity in topological semimetal YPtBi
articles.titleEn: Resilient j = 3/2 superconductivity in topological semimetal YPtBi
articles.abstract: Cooper pairing in most of the known fermionic superfluids occurs via spin-1/2 quasiparticle interactions that lead to spin-singlet or spin-triplet pairing. In the topological semimetal YPtBi, strong spin–orbit coupling results in a band inversion between highly symmetric s - and p -like electronic bands and a degeneracy at the Γ point that ensures the manifold of j = 3/2 quasiparticle states thrive near the Fermi level, where superconducting pairing occurs. Here we study the effects of magnetic and nonmagnetic disorder and carrier density on this exotic superconducting pairing state. By varying levels of disorder and carrier densities by nearly two and three orders of magnitude, respectively, we show that the superconducting critical temperature of YPtBi has a remarkable robustness, with little variation across this span. Our results suggest that superconductivity in YPtBi may reside in a regime where phase stiffness, rather than pair formation, governs the transition temperature. The insensitivity of Cooper pairing to dramatic changes in quasiparticle environment in a j = 3/2 superconductor highlights a form of protection realized in topological high-spin superconductors.

articles.title: Durable CD8-mediated remission after brief anti-HIV-1 antibody treatment requires FcγR engagement
articles.titleEn: Durable CD8-mediated remission after brief anti-HIV-1 antibody treatment requires FcγR engagement
articles.abstract: Despite highly efficacious antiretroviral therapy (ART), durable ART-free remission remains a central objective of HIV-1 cure strategies. The randomized, placebo-controlled RIO trial recently demonstrated that long-acting broadly neutralizing anti-HIV-1 antibodies (bNAbs) can sustain prolonged virologic control after ART interruption, including control that persisted beyond the period of therapeutically relevant antibody concentrations, providing clinical evidence consistent with host-mediated suppression. However, the mechanisms underlying these “vaccinal” effects remain unresolved. Here, we establish Fcγ receptor (FcγR) engagement as an essential driver of multiyear remission after bNAb therapy in simian-human immunodeficiency virus (SHIV)-infected macaques. Brief therapy during acute infection with Fc domain variants of the bNAb 3BNC117, matched for antigen binding, neutralizing activity, and pharmacokinetics but differing in FcγR engagement, produced comparable early virologic control yet profoundly divergent long-term outcomes. Sustained CD8 T cell–dependent suppression lasting nearly 300 wk developed in every evaluable animal receiving the FcγR-engaging variant but arose in only one of eight recipients of the FcγR-null variant. FcγR-driven immunomodulation imprinted a CD8 T cell response characterized by enhanced antigen-specific effector function, early clonal focusing with sustained clonotype persistence, and distinct cellular-state transcriptional signatures. Our findings identify the Fc–FcγR axis as a critical determinant of the reliable induction of durable remission and provide a mechanistic framework for developing Fc-engineered bNAbs designed to enhance vaccinal immunity and advance antibody-based strategies with the potential to achieve functional cure.

articles.title: Nutritional niches reveal mutualism resilience in urban fungus-farming ants
articles.titleEn: Nutritional niches reveal mutualism resilience in urban fungus-farming ants
articles.abstract: Maintaining optimized nutrient exchange between partnered species across changing environments presents a fundamental challenge for nutritional mutualisms. Yet quantitative approaches linking nutrient acquisition by one partner with the nutritional requirements of the other have been lacking. Here we extend the Nutritional Geometry Framework from organisms and colonies to interspecific mutualisms by linking realized nutritional niches (RNNs) with nutritional performance landscapes to quantify nutritional homeostasis between interacting species. Nutritional analyses of thousands of DNA-barcoded plant fragments collected by free-ranging Panamanian leafcutter ants revealed that RNNs for fungal cultivar provisioning diverged between degraded urban and intact rainforest habitats. Despite this, colonies converged on similar nutritional intake targets that were similarly positioned relative to regions of high fungal performance, while fungal nutritional yield remained stable across habitats. These findings demonstrate that correspondence between colony nutritional intake and fungal nutritional performance provides a quantitative means of assessing nutritional homeostasis across interacting species and establishes a foundation for comparative analyses of nutrient exchange across mutualisms experiencing environmental change.

articles.title: Molecular interactions underlying selective partitioning of clients into MED1 and FUS condensates
articles.titleEn: Molecular interactions underlying selective partitioning of clients into MED1 and FUS condensates
articles.abstract: Biomolecular condensates selectively recruit and exclude proteins, and this partitioning is sometimes dictated by their intrinsically disordered regions. Factors that determine partitioning include client–scaffold interactions and stabilization of the scaffold network within the condensate, yet a molecular and predictive understanding has not been fully achieved. Here, we used coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate molecular interactions between two types of nuclear proteins as scaffolds: the charge-rich disordered region of Mediator 1 (MED1) and the aromatic-rich disordered region of Fused in Sarcoma (FUS), in mixtures with client intrinsically disordered regions from six different proteins. We show distinct partitioning into the MED1 and FUS condensates, while the presence of RNA in both dilute and dense phases modulated client partitioning. Favorable client–scaffold interaction energies within condensates were associated with client partitioning, while client–scaffold interactions competed with scaffold self-interactions. Analysis of interaction energies of individual residues revealed that the interactions were localized to specific sequence regions: charged blocks for interactions with MED1, and dispersed aromatic residues for interactions with FUS. Using residue–resolved interaction energies from our molecular dynamics simulations, we developed sequence-based predictors of client partitioning into MED1 and FUS condensates. Our prediction approach for partitioning can be extended to other biomolecules, offering a framework to analyze their partitioning in cellular environments.

articles.title: The ocean–atmosphere turbulent flux algorithm in E3SMv2 does not always converge to unique and physical solutions: analysis and potential remedy
articles.titleEn: The ocean–atmosphere turbulent flux algorithm in E3SMv2 does not always converge to unique and physical solutions: analysis and potential remedy
articles.abstract: The development of physics parameterizations in Earth system models typically emphasizes whether the intended physics is reasonably represented, while mathematical aspects such as solvability of the governing equations and convergence of the numerical algorithms used to approximate their solutions receive far less attention. In this work, we examine these mathematical issues for a widely used ocean–atmosphere turbulent flux parameterization and its implementation in the Energy Exascale Earth System Model version 2 (E3SMv2). We show that, under simulated meteorological conditions, the parameterization can yield no solution or multiple (including unintended) solutions. These problems arise primarily from (1) a discontinuity in the formulation of the neutral exchange coefficients and (2) the use of an ad hoc limiter on the Monin–Obukhov length to address a singularity in its definition. Compounding these problems is the fact that interventions such as limiters are often thought to have only a “minor” effect on numerical algorithms and are not documented in technical model descriptions. To address these solvability issues, we propose (1) a regularization that enforces continuity in the neutral exchange coefficients and (2) an adaptive procedure for selecting limiting values of the Monin–Obukhov length based on mathematical analysis of solution uniqueness. Implementing these revisions in E3SMv2 leads to statistically significant changes in the simulated latent heat fluxes over the mid-latitude oceans in the winter hemisphere as well as over the subtropical and tropical oceans. Overall, this work improves the well-posedness and numerical accuracy of ocean–atmosphere turbulent flux calculations in E3SMv2. Moreover, because discontinuities and ad hoc limiters are frequently encountered in physics parameterizations, this work serves as an example of how non-existence and non-uniqueness issues in parameterizations can be identified, analyzed, and resolved.

articles.title: Development of AC FIRE version 1.0: a mesoscale model with forest canopy and fire behavior submodels
articles.titleEn: Development of AC FIRE version 1.0: a mesoscale model with forest canopy and fire behavior submodels
articles.abstract: Numerical models are essential for advancing understanding of fire–atmosphere interactions, especially where field campaigns alone cannot provide sufficient insight. Existing wildland fire models vary greatly in complexity and scale, from computational fluid dynamics models with detailed combustion submodels, to mesoscale models with empirical or semi-empirical combustion representations, to global or regional models that omit combustion byproducts altogether. However, no existing frameworks simultaneously represent atmospheric responses to wildland fires across scales from hundreds of meters to hundreds of kilometers, incorporate a comprehensive suite of physical parameterizations, and explicitly resolve some scales of atmospheric turbulence within and above a forest canopy. To address this gap, we introduce ARPS-CANOPY/DEVS-FIRE (hereafter, AC FIRE ), a mesoscale model that integrates a canopy resolving atmospheric model (ARPS-CANOPY) with a surface fire behavior model (DEVS-FIRE) and detail its development and preliminary evaluation. Unlike the original ARPS-CANOPY, which relied on a user-imposed fire heat source, AC FIRE employs two-way fire-atmosphere coupling to compute heat release from a surface fire dynamically. We demonstrate the coupled modeling system with a low-intensity prescribed fire conducted in the New Jersey Pine Barrens in March 2019. We compare simulated atmospheric variables to corresponding flux tower observations and simulated fire spread rates with measurements from an array of surface thermocouples deployed during the fire. The 30-m horizontal grid spacing in this preliminary AC FIRE study allows explicit resolution of some convective turbulent motions above the canopy, while turbulence within and near the canopy is parameterized. The AC FIRE simulation generally captures the mean and turbulent flow through the forest canopy and substantially improves upon ARPS-CANOPY with an imposed heat source in its representation of upper-canopy TKE. The simulated spread rates compare favorably to observed spread rates, with differences attributable at least partially to the use of uniform fuels in the AC FIRE simulation. Although the present framework is limited to surface-fire behavior and does not simulate torching or crown-fire propagation, the integration of a dynamically coupled fire heat source represents a significant advance in canopy-resolving mesoscale modeling. Beyond this initial case, AC FIRE provides a foundation for investigating a broader range of wildland fire–atmosphere interactions and for future development of more comprehensive fire–canopy coupling and operational applications.

articles.title: Evaluation of precipitation variability over complex terrain based on observations and high resolution WRF v4.2.2 modelling
articles.titleEn: Evaluation of precipitation variability over complex terrain based on observations and high resolution WRF v4.2.2 modelling
articles.abstract: Heterogeneity in the occurrence, amount and distribution of precipitation in mountainous areas is relevant for water resources and stresses the need for high-altitude observations and high-resolution modeling over complex terrain. This work focuses on the analysis of precipitation in the Sierra de Guadarrama, a mountain range at the center of the Iberian Plateau that provides water resources for several million citizens living within it and in nearby cities, mostly Madrid. The precipitation climatology is assessed from available observations and high resolution climate model simulations during the period 1991–2020. For this purpose, data from 37 stations located in the Sierra de Guadarrama and surrounding lowlands, with altitudes ranging from 600 to 2200 ma.s.l. have been analyzed and compared to model simulations. A regional simulation with the WRF model (version 4.2.2), driven with boundary conditions provided by the ERA5 reanalysis, was performed. The simulation has three nested domains with increasing resolutions of 9, 3, and 1 km, with the smallest domain covering the target region, including the Sierra de Guadarrama and surroundings. The comparison of the different data sources aims at characterizing the precipitation distribution over the area, assessing the performance of ERA5 and the potential added value of the increasing resolution of the WRF simulation in reproducing the observations. Results show that the increase in WRF resolution from 9 to 3 km produces a better representation of the overall climatology of precipitation and the altitudinal gradients. The 1 km resolution simulation represents better the shape of the probability distribution of precipitation, including extremes, but overestimates total accumulations, mostly due to an overestimation of the occurrence of wet days. Orography plays a very relevant role in activating precipitation and precipitation gradients with altitude are best captured at 1 km resolution, as well as extreme values. However, some seasonal gradients are best matched by the 3 km resolution. Furthermore, summer convective precipitation is slightly improved, but still poorly simulated, likely because the simulation does not allow for convection-permitting at any resolution. The results are discussed with the support of some sensitivity tests changing convection parameterizations and allowing for convection-permitting schemes (CPS). The results are relevant to understand the behavior of precipitation in complex terrain, to better interpret mountain climates and also the hydrology of the center of the Iberian Peninsula.
